conditions.text: Set up the reported environment: app version 1.4.0 on iOS 18.4, device iPhone15,2 — all three reported by Sentry contexts in every event.
Push must be in a non-deliverable state with OS-level permission DENIED; both hold in all events.
Push provider registration is not a fixed condition: 2 events were REGISTERED and 1 was STALE.
Profile consistency also varies and so is not required: one event true, one false, one UNKNOWN.
How the user arrives at the settings screen does not matter: one event came via /home then /settings, one via foreground then /inbox, and one after a 97-step prefix of paging through /search/results.
Note that breadcrumbs were truncated in 1 event, so its full prefix is not fully known.
No suspect commit was identified, so there is no specific change to revert or bisect against from this packet.

missing_evidence_questions.text: What exactly is null at src/modules/push/permission.ts:27 — the response object from POST /api/push/permission, or some other value whose 'status' is read?
Why does POST /api/push/permission return 403, and is the 403 a required trigger or merely correlated with OS permission being DENIED?
Does the crash still reproduce with provider registration STALE versus REGISTERED, given the split across events?
What is the real value of profile.consistent in the event where it is UNKNOWN, and does it affect reproduction at all?
Can the truncated breadcrumb trail for the affected event be recovered to confirm no additional step is required?
Which change introduced the null-handling path in requestPermission, since suspect commit analysis returned NONE_FOUND?
Does the crash reproduce on app versions, iOS versions or devices other than 1.4.0 / iOS 18.4 / iPhone15,2, which are the only ones observed?

steps_prose.text: Navigate to /settings/notifications; this step is present in all 3 events considered.
Tap the button#enable-push control on that screen, also seen in every event.
The app issues POST /api/push/permission, which responds 403 in all events.

The crash then surfaces as TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status') in requestPermission at src/modules/push/permission.ts line 27; the packet does not describe the code path between the 403 and the null read, so treat that link as unconfirmed.

summary.text: Across 3 events, a TypeError "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status')" is thrown in requestPermission at src/modules/push/permission.ts:27 when a user enables push from the notification settings screen and the backend permission call returns 403.
